messages:
alex: Noticing a spike in GPU evictions in us-west-3 after last night's microcode/BMC push. Nodes are hitting thermal throttle and failing provisioning. Anyone else seeing this?

ops-bot: deploy-bmc-microcode v1.4.2 completed for racks: usw3-rack-a, usw3-rack-b at 2026-03-17T02:10:12Z :white_check_mark:

maria: Saw it. Dedicated pool provisioning failures up ~12% since 02:15 UTC. Jobs keep retrying and autoscaler is launching extra hosts.

jon: Which hosts? Can you paste a sample dmesg/journal from an affected host (r-usw3-gpu-42) so we can see the OOM/thermal messages?

sara: grabbing logs now. here's the kernel snippet from r-usw3-gpu-42: 
```
Mar 17 02:16:08 r-usw3-gpu-42 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 17 02:16:08 r-usw3-gpu-42 kernel: thermal: critical temperature reached (nvme0: 105C)
Mar 17 02:16:09 r-usw3-gpu-42 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 17 02:16:10 r-usw3-gpu-42 kernel: bmc-fw: secure_boot_attr changed from 0->1 during last-flash
```

cheng: Interesting — the v1.4.2 manifest contained a secure-boot attribute flip for some BMC builds (was a non-intentional flag in the vendor's image). If the BMC toggled UEFI lockdown semantics it can affect thermal/pgc interactions for our BIOS microcode handler. Not saying it's the only cause but it's correlated to the timeline.

leo: Mitigation plan: 1) Pause rollout (staged already?) 2) Rollback to v1.4.1 on canary racks 3) Cordon affected hosts from provisioning pools 4) Disable autoscaler scale-ups to avoid cost spike. I'll start rollback on rack-a canary now.

alex: Can we cordon those nodes and drain any provisioning pods to stop requeue churn? e.g. 
```
kubectl cordon r-usw3-gpu-42
kubectl drain r-usw3-gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

maria: Doing cordon/drain on the visible ones. Also FYI finance flagged a 9% infra spike last hour due to retries. I'll dump the autoscaler events and post in #finance-ops.

jon: Runbook check: after rollback we should validate BMC secure-boot flag, NVMe and GPU thermal sensors, and confirm no OOB session drops. Commands I run for checks: 
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P **** fru
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC sdr elist
journalctl -k -b -1 | grep -i thermal
```

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-443. Pager escalation: oncall -> cheng -> leo.

sara: I'll capture timeline + affected capacity in a quick postmortem. For immediate next steps: pause microcode rollouts, rollback canary, cordon/evict. After rollback we should run a small provisioning canary (2 instances) and watch for throttles for 30m. :white_check_mark:

leo: rollback started on usw3-rack-a (r-usw3-gpu-40..45). ETA ~12m. I also disabled auto-rollout in the firmware pipeline.

maria: Added cost notes to INC-2026-443 and pinged finance.

alex: Thanks — please @mention me when canary is green or if we see repeated secure-boot flips.

sara: Will follow up with a short root-cause note and next steps. For now pausing all BMC microcode pushes globally until we validate the vendor build. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
